assets.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: full-bleed 16:9 conference slide illustration. New artwork for a software supply-chain security talk, consistent with an existing hand-inked workshop/dispatch-warehouse cartoon style. Bold elegant contour lines, restrained halftone and textured paper, deep petrol and graphite shadows, warm ivory and amber practical lamps, restrained burgundy and coral attacker accent. Composition: LEFT 44 percent nearly empty deep charcoal-petrol shadow for large editable slide text. RIGHT 56 percent contains the storytelling scene, with safe crop margins. A legitimate maintainer's small workshop workstation, seen in three-quarter view, displays a very convincing friendly group video meeting as a small theatrical scene inside its monitor. One apparently helpful maintenance plug/tool extends from that staged meeting toward the desk. Behind the monitor a small sly coral segmented worm in a charcoal wool cap is quietly drawing the WORKSHOP'S EXISTING brass publishing key from its hook along the maintenance cable. The key's hook connects visibly to a parcel dispatch stamping machine on the same bench, and two small ordinary parcels wait there. Focus on the social lure borrowing an existing identity; no explosion, no giant monster. The false meeting looks inviting while a subtle paper-theatre backing reveals deception. Human silhouettes in the screen only, no real people or likenesses. A coherent tangible illustration rather than floating symbols or an infographic. No readable text, lettering, numbers, logos, watermarks, shields, neon locks, hooded hackers, dashboards or fake code. Cinematic editorial lighting and strong silhouettes. Entire LEFT text area stays quiet and dark, not filled by objects.

Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: full-bleed 16:9 conference slide illustration. New hand-inked editorial artwork in a tactile software dispatch-workshop world: bold confident contours, restrained halftone and paper grain, graphite and deep petrol shadow, amber lamps, brass hardware, kraft packages, burgundy cable, small coral attacker accent. LEFT 44 percent is quiet almost-empty charcoal-petrol darkness for editable title and three short evidence lines. RIGHT 56 percent is one clear physical story. On a workshop bench, an opened ordinary dependency parcel has a little coral segmented worm in a charcoal cap half-hidden inside. A real brass access key lies on a short transport rail leading from the parcel to a tall developer-editor console with a removable plug-in cartridge. The worm has guided the key to the console's existing release mechanism; the console is now inserting a matching cartridge back into a second workstation slot. A thin burgundy conduit runs from that cartridge toward the second workstation's existing key drawer, subtly showing the credential route. Make the dependency-package to editor-extension connection visually legible with only these few connected objects. Monitor screen is an abstract blank editor plane, no invented interface or text. No corporate victim, network of hundreds of nodes, fake dashboards, neon locks, shields, logos, numbers, letters, captions, watermark or hooded hacker. Use an intimate three-quarter camera and crafted warm lighting. The illustration is a mechanism metaphor, not forensic evidence. Keep all important objects inside right-side safe margins and the left text area calm.

Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: very wide 16:9 full-slide background for a software supply-chain incident overview. New hand-inked editorial panorama matching a tactile dark dispatch-workshop world: bold elegant contours, restrained halftone and paper texture, charcoal/petrol steel, warm amber lamps, ivory paper, burgundy cable, tiny coral accents. Composition is specifically for native editable text: TOP 0-20 percent is dark calm negative space for a large title. Across the MIDDLE band, approximately y=20-48 percent, show a continuous cutaway workshop with FOUR visually distinct but connected still-life areas evenly distributed left to right: (1) a parcel receiving shelf full of varied kraft dependency boxes; (2) an archive cabinet of assorted code/library modules and a solid release crate; (3) a mechanical build and dispatch press with hanging blank work tickets; (4) a developer workstation with a plug-in cartridge and a small open instruction notebook. These are connected by ordinary brass rails and burgundy cable, not glowing graph lines. No people or mascot foreground. The BOTTOM HALF y=50-100 percent must remain consistently deep quiet petrol darkness with only a very faint continuation of structural shadows, because four columns of 32 incident names will be placed there as editable text. Show tangible breadth of a toolchain, not numerical prevalence; no repeated objects purporting to count incidents. Make the middle-band objects large and readable as silhouettes, with depth and atmospheric warmth. No readable text, letters, numbers, logos, titles, panels, charts, cybersecurity grids, blue neon, locks, shields, watermarks or pseudo-UI. Avoid filling the bottom half with bright objects.
